scope: Reuse the album editor's actual mobile and web interfaces for each feed photo, and publish four distinct decorated posts through four new content author accounts.

editor.sharedAppearance: Existing album stage colors, typography, icons, selected states, tool sheets and workspace layout are reused directly.
preservation: The current album edit session and undo history remain isolated.
The original photo cannot be deleted through tool panels or keyboard shortcuts.
Account changes close active tools and discard stale results.
Photo artwork remains editable when transferred into an album; the separate feed caption is excluded.
Existing non-500-width artwork retains its canvas, positions and font sizes across stage, thumbnail, crop preview and save.
editor.inputValidation: Feed precision coordinates are checked against the portable document bounds before committing; ordinary album entry keeps its existing behavior.
singlePhotoConstraints: Multi-photo layout and template actions explain their album-specific use.
The existing portable asset contract remains unchanged: eight free procedural stickers, emoji text, and entitled image frames.

content.profiles: Each account has its own bio and prepared profile photo.
content.artwork: Four visually reviewed 1152x1440 PNGs with separate editable design documents and feed captions.
verified: All four posts appear in anonymous feed and detail queries.
Public snapshots and profile photos match the reviewed local PNG hashes.
Private originals and editable design JSON match the prepared documents.
Public responses do not expose the private original paths or design layers.
Existing profiles, record and post retain identical row hashes; albums remain at 20.

validation.independentReadOnlyReview: Two coordinate-related findings fixed and covered by focused regression checks.

knownGoldenMismatch.location: Selected template icon and label only; geometry and remaining pixels match.

delivery.clientReleaseNote: The new editor interface requires an app release. Content is already published independently of that client release.

resourceUse: Focused checks used the existing Flutter runtime, low process priority and concurrency 1. New heavy jobs waited for other active builds; an unrelated test started after our final test batch had already begun. No other task's process or data was stopped or removed.
